items.title: Euler formula for connected plane multigraphs
items.statement: Every finite nonempty connected polygonal plane multigraph, allowing loops and parallel edges, satisfies V-E+F=2; the zero-edge connected case is included.
items.strategy: Subdivide each loop and each parallel edge twice using fresh vertices. The point-set drawing and faces stay fixed, while the resulting graph is finite, simple, connected, and plane; compare its vertex and edge counts with the original.

references.title: R. Diestel, Graph Theory, 6th ed., Theorem 4.2.9

items.title: Planar-diagram, Gauss, and signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite codes
items.statement: Defines normalized Gauss, signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite, and oriented planar-diagram codes, including incidence, sign, parity, face, outer-face, and crossingless-orientation conditions.
items.strategy: Define the three finite encodings and fix their normalization and sign conventions explicitly. Keep the signed DT code knot-specific and distinguish local syntactic validity from spherical realizability.

references.title: Erickson, Planar Graphs, Computational Topology lecture notes, 2023, sections Rotation Systems and Formalities and Trivialities
Knot Atlas, Gauss Codes and Planar Diagrams manuals

items.title: Realizability and face validation for planar-diagram codes
items.statement: A nonempty connected oriented four-valent rotation-system code with valid strand, overpass, and crossing-sign data is realizable on the sphere exactly when its face permutation satisfies Euler characteristic two; a distinguished face specifies the plane model, and the two oriented crossingless codes are handled separately.
items.strategy: Construct a polygonal sphere embedding from a spanning tree, then add the remaining paired edges. Each edge changes the face-cycle count by one; the Euler equality forces each step to split one face. Cap crossing disks and edge bands and lift the overpass data.
items.axiom_base: Finite rotation-system realization and face-count argument are choice-free; the planned Countable Choice dependency is under review because the local construction does not use it.

items.title: Planar-code validation and diagram reconstruction
items.statement: Checks a finite oriented planar-diagram code in a fixed order, returns the first specific invalid-code reason, or constructs its decorated plane diagram and face data.
items.strategy: Scan incidence and orientation records, construct the rotation and edge-pairing permutations, check each crossing and component condition, count face cycles, test Euler characteristic two, then build crossing disks and edge bands.

references.title: Hass, Lagarias, and Pippenger, The Computational Complexity of Knot and Link Problems, 1999, sections 1 and 7
Erickson, Planar Graphs, Computational Topology lecture notes, 2023, sections Rotation Systems and Formalities and Trivialities

items.title: Enumerate diagram codes up to a crossing bound
items.statement: Given a nonnegative crossing bound, enumerates normalized connected one-component diagram codes through the bound, including both oriented crossingless codes, and returns reconstructed diagram candidates rather than knot types.
items.strategy: For each crossing count in the finite range, enumerate every normalized pairing, crossing rotation, orientation, overpass assignment, and outer-face selector; retain exactly the inputs accepted by the validator.

references.title: Hass, Lagarias, and Pippenger, The Computational Complexity of Knot and Link Problems, 1999, sections 1 and 7

items.title: Planar-code validation and reconstruction procedure properties
items.statement: For every admissible encoded input of the planar-code validation algorithm, the finite procedure terminates, rejects exactly the listed syntax and realizability failures, and otherwise returns the prescribed reconstructed diagram and face data.
items.strategy: Bound every scan by the finite code size, prove each rejection branch matches its named failed predicate, and use the realizability lemma for the final acceptance branch.

references.title: Hass, Lagarias, and Pippenger, The Computational Complexity of Knot and Link Problems, 1999, section 1

items.title: Enumeration of diagrams up to a crossing bound procedure properties
items.statement: For every nonnegative crossing bound, the finite enumeration procedure terminates and returns exactly the reconstructed candidates represented by its normalized connected knot-diagram codes up to that bound.
items.strategy: Count the finite code space at each crossing count, use the strict bound to make the outer loop finite, and apply the validator procedure theorem to every candidate.

references.title: Hass, Lagarias, and Pippenger, The Computational Complexity of Knot and Link Problems, 1999, sections 1 and 7
Erickson, Planar Graphs, Computational Topology lecture notes, 2023, sections Rotation Systems and Formalities and Trivialities

items.title: Valid codes reconstruct the declared link diagram
items.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, a valid connected one-component oriented code reconstructs its declared diagram, is unique up to planar isotopy and relabeling, and its normalized code appears among candidates at its crossing count; the smooth-isotopy uniqueness proof is escalated.
items.strategy: Use the local face-realization result and deterministic reconstruction, align the finite crossing disks and edge bands, isotope corresponding arcs within each disk face, extend the finite arc isotopies, and use the outer-face datum to pass from the sphere to the plane.
items.axiom_base: The combinatorial realization and enumeration clause are choice-free. The smooth ambient-isotopy clause uses Countable Choice through the published smooth disk arc-isotopy extension supplier.

items.title: A crossing label occurring once is invalid
items.statement: The one-entry word -1 with declared crossing count 1 has its only label present but violates the required two-visit condition and is rejected before graph or face tests.
items.strategy: Use the one-entry word with label 1, count its visits, and identify the validator's first failed crossing-incidence test.

items.title: Trefoil Gauss traversal and rotation reconstruction
items.statement: The based signed Gauss word -1,3,-2,1,-3,2 with crossing signs (+1,+1,+1) gives the right trefoil; its normalized PD rows, five face cycles, selected outer face, and bound-three enumeration inclusion are checked explicitly.
items.strategy: Trace the six signed visits, verify the edge and crossing incidences, compute the face permutation and Euler characteristic, select the outer face, and verify the finite enumerator includes the normalized code at bound three.
items.axiom_base: The finite code and enumeration checks are choice-free; the reconstruction up to smooth planar isotopy inherits Countable Choice from the theorem supplier.
